office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 41st District (Mercer Island, Newcastle and parts of Bellevue, Issaquah, Renton and Sammamish), voting on state law, budgets and taxes for two-year terms.
race_blurb: Incumbent Democrat Janice Zahn, appointed in 2025 and a former Bellevue councilmember, faces Republican Elle Nguyen, who opposes a state income tax and the 2026 state housing-siting mandate. Zahn took 72% in the August primary.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2025 and former Bellevue councilmember (2017-2025); Port of Seattle chief engineer running on affordability, infrastructure investment and fiscal responsibility.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million (ESSB 6346), the tax I-645 would repeal [S8]
Voted for 2025 rent stabilization (EHB 1217) and the 2026 supportive-housing siting law (ESHB 2266) [S9][S10]
Says Washington must 'accelerate investments in clean energy and community resilience' to meet 2030 climate goals [S4]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), the parents' rights amendments I-1 would undo; no public position found on the three initiatives [S7]

taxes.basis: Voted yea on ESSB 6346, the 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million; no further stated tax agenda.

spending.basis: Pairs 'delivering investments in housing, education, childcare, and transportation' with 'fiscal responsibility' and 'accountability' on budget challenges: genuinely mixed.

housing.basis: Voted for 2025 rent stabilization and for ESHB 2266 requiring cities to allow supportive housing and shelters.

climate.basis: Says the state must accelerate clean-energy investment to meet 2030 climate goals; endorsed by Conservation Action.

experience.basis: Sitting legislator since 2025 with eight prior years on the Bellevue council: an established record, though short legislative tenure.

local-control.basis: Voted for ESHB 2266, which requires cities to allow transitional and supportive housing and shelters in specified zones.

social.basis: Pamphlet endorsement list includes Planned Parenthood; no direct statement on gender or reproductive policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yea on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; single vote, no statement.

candidates.summary: Republican challenger from Mercer Island, a real estate investor and community advocate without prior elected office, running on fiscal discipline, public safety and local control.
highlights: Opposes a state income tax and says 'Olympia has been fiscally irresponsible' [S4]
'Adamantly opposes' ESHB 2266: 'Olympia should not substitute statewide mandates for the judgment of local communities' [S4]
Site lists 'Supporting law enforcement, holding criminals accountable' [S3]
States a commitment to 'parental rights' without specifics; no public position found on the three initiatives [S4]

taxes.basis: Opposes a state income tax and lists 'protecting taxpayers from unnecessary tax increases'.

spending.basis: Repeated calls for fiscal discipline, stopping wasteful spending and balancing the budget; says Olympia has been fiscally irresponsible.

safety.basis: Site lists supporting law enforcement and holding criminals accountable; no detailed enforcement agenda.

experience.basis: No elected office held; prior unsuccessful school-board and legislative runs.

local-control.basis: Adamantly opposes ESHB 2266 as a statewide mandate overriding 'the judgment of local communities'; commits to 'meaningful local control'.

parental-rights.basis: Repeatedly names 'parental rights' as a commitment, but no specific position on notification, curricula or opt-outs.
